test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the key reason governments promote Public-Private Partnerships in infrastructure development?

options.text: To address fiscal constraints and reduce liabilities
To improve efficiency and innovation through private sector expertise
Due to lack of trained manpower

solution:
The correct answer is __**To improve efficiency and innovation through private sector expertise**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) leverage the **expertise, efficiency, and innovation** of the private sector to address infrastructure needs.
 
• Private sector involvement often leads to **better project delivery timelines** and reduced costs due to advanced technology and effective management practices.
 
• PPPs foster **innovation in financing, construction, and operation** by allowing private entities to bring in modern solutions.
 
• Governments aim to ensure **quality infrastructure services** while minimizing financial risks and burdens on the public sector.
 
• This model enhances **accountability and transparency** in large-scale infrastructure projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public-Private Partnership (PPP):** A collaborative model where public and private sectors share resources, risks, and rewards to deliver public infrastructure or services.
 
• **Efficiency in PPPs:** The private sector’s operational expertise ensures faster project delivery and reduced lifecycle costs.
 
• **Risk Sharing:** In PPP arrangements, risks such as financial, technical, and operational risks are shared between the government and private entities.
 
• **Types of PPP Models:** Common models include Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT), Design-Build-Finance-Operate (DBFO), and Build-Own-Operate (BOO).
 
• **Global Examples:** Successful PPP projects include the London Underground modernization and the Delhi Metro Rail in India.
